content.title: About
content.content: Tommy Atkins mango is one of the most popular mango varieties, known for its sweet, aromatic flavor and bright orange flesh. The fruits are usually large, with a smooth skin that turns slightly yellow when ripe. This product is peeled and pitted, presented raw and ready to eat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Tommy Atkins cultivar was developed in the United States in the 1940s and became the world’s most exported mango variety.
Mango is considered the “king of fruits” in India and Southeast Asia.
A single fruit can weigh between 300 and 800 g and contains up to 20 % sugar.
Mango skin contains enzymes that can break down tissues, which is why it is usually not eaten.
Mango seeds are rich in antioxidants, but they are not consumed raw.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Mango provides a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin A and beta‑carotene
items.content: The orange flesh is abundant in beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A important for vision and skin health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in mango aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Beneficial antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in mango help combat free radicals.

items.title: Heart‑supporting potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to mango, especially those sensitive to latex cross‑reactivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Mango is relatively sweet, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Enzyme irritation
items.content: Raw mango juice can irritate skin and mucous membranes in sensitive persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peeled mango can be eaten fresh, added to smoothies, salads, desserts, yogurt, or used in sauces. It can also be cubed and frozen for homemade ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peeled mango in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze the pieces in a freezer‑safe bag – they retain flavor and nutrients for up to 6 months.
